channel.title: World News
channel.description: Aggregated headlines linking to original publishers

item.title: US economy grew more than expected in 3rd quarter, government data shows
item.description: The United States economy expanded at an annualized rate of 3.4% over the three months ending in September, according to a government report released on Thursday.

item.title: ECB President Lagarde steps down in order to speak out
item.description: European Central Bank President Christine Lagarde will step down from her post several months early, in order to have more "freedom to engage on matters that are not monetary policy." The comments will fuel speculation about her future plans, ahead of a presidential election in her native France. The resignation also sparks a succession race, as Europe faces a turbulent fiscal future. Also in the show - oil giant TotalEnergies reports record profits as the EU warns on household energy bills.

item.title: Midterm elections live updates: Trump rallies voters in South Carolina
item.description: Trump spoke at a campaign event in Rock Hill, South Carolina.

item.title: Patrick Stewart, star of 'Star Trek' and 'X men', dies at 86
item.description: The British actor Patrick Stewart has died at 86, a statement released on Thursday said. Stewart was an acclaimed actor in Britain with the Royal Shakespeare Company before he starred in the beloved sci-fi TV show "Star Trek" in the 80s and later in the "X-Men" franchise.

item.title: 'Extremist right-wing ideologies' an increasing threat in France & 'across much of democratic world'
item.description: François Picard is pleased to welcome Dr Joseph Downing, Senior Lecturer in International Relations and Politics at Aston University. In modern France, the politics of insecurity increasingly extends beyond questions of crime and public order to encompass deeper struggles over national identity, disappearance of the political centre and erosion of democratic values. The emergence of far-right extremist violence, alongside the persistent stigmatization of ethnically diverse working-class suburbs, raises urgent questions about the relationship between fiery and divisive political rhetoric and far-right radicalization. Downing examines these interrelated challenges against the backdrop of a deadly shooting in the Paris suburbs, allegedly motivated by racist and anti-Muslim hostility.

item.title: What killed 500-plus penguins? How scientists solved the mystery
item.description: The penguins that perished lived on the Danger Islands in Antarctica. The prime suspect was avian flu. Researchers were surprised by what they found.

item.title: Lost your spark? The "silent sister" of depression, and a quiz to spot her
item.description: Always busy, but rarely joyful? Allison Aubrey and Juana Summers discuss a tool to spot "high functioning depression."

item.title: Star Trek and X-Men star Sir Patrick Stewart dies
item.description: Star Trek and X-Men actor Sir Patrick Stewart has died after a "brief and poignant journey" with Alzheimer's and dementia.

item.title: Judge blocks Trump administration's Medicaid rule forcing sick recipients to prove frailty
item.description: A federal judge has ruled that chronically ill people on Medicaid won’t be bound by new work requirement rules that the latest Trump administration guidance requires in order to qualify for “medically frail” exemptions

item.title: Michigan's El-Sayed targeted by Republicans in Midterms race: Will the religion card work?
item.description: What in the name of political free speech is off-limits? Can you say whatever you want on the campaign trail, no matter how false or racist?

item.title: French shooting suspect deliberately targeted Muslims, Africans
item.description: A man suspected of a gun attack in the Paris suburbs last week, killing one person and wounding seven including a child, has admitted to "targeting individuals who appeared to be Muslim, African, or North African," prosecutors said on Thursday. The attack came amid an increasingly tense political climate, with just six months to go before next spring's presidential election.

item.title: DOJ issues new wave of subpoenas in criminal probe of Alaska Senate race, sources say
item.description: The DOJ is issuing new subpoenas in a probe of Alaska's U.S. Senate race and alleged efforts by Democrats to recruit a candidate with the same name as the GOP incumbent.

item.title: 'Deeply regressive': How the French government plans to make protesters pay for riots and looting
item.description: As France continues to pick up the pieces after riots and looting broke out on the fringes of nationwide peaceful demonstrations on October 17, the government is pushing forward a bill that would make protesters have to pay up to €10,000 in reparations for damage caused during public unrest – even if they were not directly responsible for the vandalism.

item.title: Lt. Gen. Ben Hodges accuses Hegseth of 'getting rid of people who may have the courage to push back'
item.description: Erin Ogunkeye welcomes Lt. General (ret.) Ben Hodges, former commander of US Army Europe and NATO Allied Land Command. The dismissal of senior military officers without public explanation raises fundamental questions about institutional trust and the relationship between civilian authority and military leadership. For General Hodges, the reported firing of Lt. General Brett Sylvia reflects a potentially troubling pattern within the Pentagon under Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth. Equally striking is his criticism of the reluctance of retired senior commanders to speak publicly against policies they consider damaging. Hodges said he was "disappointed and surprised" by the limited public resistance among former four-star generals.

item.title: Even birds get jet lagged, study shows
item.description: A species of seabirds appears to become disoriented on flights back to its nest due to shifting time zones.

item.title: 'An absurdity' to blame human error: Spain's deadly train crash 'should never' have happened
item.description: Following Spain's deadly high-speed train crash, Delano D'Souza is joined by Francisco Badea, Director of FEM Expert Engineering, Railway Structural & PRM Certification Expert. Batea challenges explanations that reduce railway disasters to isolated human mistakes. “It is basically an absurdity to say that it depended on one person and one human mistake,” he argues, emphasizing that modern railway networks operate through multiple layers of protection, including automated safeguards, train-detection technologies, operational protocols and institutional oversight. “The system has been designed in a way that this type of accident should never happen.”

item.title: DR Congo: A centre celebrates the discharge of last Ebola patients
item.description: Medical staff and residents at a treatment centre in Ituri danced and sang to celebrate a first since May: the centre is no longer treating any confirmed Ebola cases.

item.title: WATCH: See National Geographic's best destinations for 2026
item.description: ABC News' Sam Champion highlights some of the must-visit places featured on National Geographic's annual list of the world's best travel destinations.

item.title: Ireland becomes refuge for anti-Trump Americans
item.description: They have left everything behind to get away from US President Donald Trump's America. Entrepreneurs, academics, scientists and students: tens of thousands of US citizens have moved to Ireland in recent years. Last year alone, some 10,000 Americans settled there and nearly 100 even applied for asylum – citing political, racial or gender persecution.

item.title: Ian McEwan speculates on 'What We Can Know' in the 22nd century
item.description: Booker Prize-winning author Ian McEwan sits down with Olivia Salazar-Winspear to discuss the 22nd century society he created in "What We Can Know", as his latest novel is translated into French. While his characters grapple with the aftermath of the great "derangement", in a world where many of the 21st century's capital cities have been submerged, we discuss our upcoming reckoning with the climate crisis.

item.title: WATCH: Obama slams Trump for getting mad at his Cheesecake Factory comment
item.description: The former president took issue with how President Donald Trump responded to his joke about "the White House looking like Saddam Hussein opened a Cheesecake Factory."

item.title: FIFA to double Women's World Cup prize money - but it doesn't match men's tournament
item.description: FIFA plans to double Women's World Cup prize money next year but will not deliver on Gianni Infantino's ambition to match the cash paid out at the men's tournament, Sky News has learnt.

item.title: Flavio Bolsonaro’s great escape: Is this the beginning of the end for ‘Bolsonarism’?
item.description: The Brazilian election results had barely been announced before the defeated presidential candidate, Flavio Bolsonaro, packed his bags and fled with his family to the United States. The move may have dealt a serious blow to the already tarnished family brand, but does it spell the end for “Bolsonarism”?

item.title: Aid mission set to enter Ukraine's Oleshky as localised ceasefire holds for third day
item.description: A humanitarian aid mission is set to enter the Ukrainian town of Oleshky, a Ukrainian official said on Thuirsday, as a localised truce between Kyiv and Moscow, brokered by US first lady Melania Trump, held for a third day. Some 2,000 residents in the Russian occupied city have been cut off from essential supplies amid reports that many are starving.

item.title: Met refers itself to police watchdog over handling of letter about Meghan's father
item.description: The Metropolitan Police has referred itself to the Independent Office for Police Conduct (IOPC) over a letter containing allegations about the Duchess of Sussex's father, Thomas Markle Snr.

item.title: A tale of two economies: How America's cost-of-living crisis is shaping US midterm elections
item.description: The economy is the number one issue for most American voters, as they worry about high food and energy costs. But can the results of November's midterm elections really impact the cost-of-living crisis? "There isn't a ton that anyone can do about it, regardless of who wins the midterms," says Greg Ip, chief economics commentator at The Wall Street Journal.

item.title: Google owner Alphabet suffers its worst-ever day on stock market - as value plunges $500bn
item.description: Shares in Google's parent company Alphabet have suffered their worst-ever day on the US stock market, falling more than 12% and knocking around half a trillion dollars off its value.

item.title: US and Japan agree to establish a Japanese facility for joint missile production
item.description: The announcement Wednesday is the latest action by the allies, who have repeatedly expressed alarm over China's growing assertiveness in Asia.

item.title: China elevates a military general to the Politburo and seeks to strengthen party discipline
item.description: This move comes about a year before President Xi Jinping is expected to secure his fourth five-year term.

item.title: WATCH: NICU babies dressed up for Halloween
item.description: The tiniest patients of the Cleveland Clinic Children's Hospital wear their first-ever Halloween costumes.

item.title: Spain's King Felipe VI and Queen Letizia visit injured in train crash at Toledo hospital
item.description: King Felipe VI and Queen Letizia arrived at Toledo University Hospital on Thursday to visit those injured in the train accident in Urda – in which at least 69 people died – who are being treated at this hospital, 15 of whom are in the ICU. The King and Queen will meet with the medical team and subsequently visit several of the injured, who will be accompanied by their families. FRANCE 24's Sarah Morris reports from oledo University Hospital.

item.title: Former church leader and wife charged with eight counts of rape
item.description: A former church leader and his wife have been charged with rape.

item.title: Ireland opens arms to Americans fleeing US President Donald Trump
item.description: Tens of thousands of US citizens have fled the United States since Donald Trump's return to power two years ago. Given the language and a shared history, Ireland has been among the top choices for Americans looking for an alternative. FRANCE 24's team reports.

item.title: Pentagon shake-up continues: US fires top army general in latest ouster
item.description: The United States has fired its top military planner, The Atlantic reported Wednesday, in a surprise shake-up as President Donald Trump appears to be preparing to resume large-scale strikes against Iran. Army Lieutenant General Brett Sylvia was removed this week from his role as head of strategy, plans and policy on the Joint Chiefs of Staff. His ouster would be the latest in a series of high-profile departures from the military since Trump returned to power a year ago.

item.title: Leaflets promoting clinics in illegal Israeli settlements handed out at London medical recruitment event
item.description: Sky News has obtained copies of leaflets promoting medical clinics in illegal Israeli settlements by a company seeking to recruit British Jewish doctors at an event in London

item.title: Food safety in India: A challenge for the world's most populous country
item.description: India's food industry feeds more than a billion people every day. But ensuring that what reaches consumers is safe has become an increasingly difficult challenge. The country has witnessed a rise in cases of food adulteration, with sometimes fatal consequences. As concerns over adulteration and poor hygiene grow, questions are being raised about whether regulators can effectively oversee such a sprawling sector.

item.title: Pentagon inspector general declines to investigate Starlink disruptions in Ukraine
item.description: The watchdog told lawmakers it was a contractual matter.

item.title: US Midterms: Donald Trump and Barack Obama make closing pitches
item.description: In the United States, Democrats are turning to Barack Obama to rally voters ahead of the midterm elections, a crucial test that could shape the remainder of Donald Trump's presidency. The former president has addressed three campaign rallies this week, with the latest one in Atlanta, Georgia. FRANCE 24's International Affairs Editor Angela Diffley has more.

item.title: Greetings from Baghdad, where Agatha Christie's old home presents its own mystery
item.description: The English writer visited Iraq multiple times in the first half of the 20th century and set some of her mystery novels there. The house in Baghdad where she once lived now sits abandoned and crumbling.

item.title: Spain reckons with second deadly train crash of the year ahead of national election
item.description: Wednesday's deadly train crash has dealt a serious blow to Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez’s campaign. The accident in Toledo province killed 69 people and came just nine months after another deadly crash on the same line, leading to accusations from experts and the public of underinvestment in railway infrastructure under Sanchez's government after years of rapid network ​expansion.

item.title: Trump and Obama trade barbs in closing week of US midterm election
item.description: Neither man is on the ​ballot but Republican President Donald Trump and Democratic former President Barack Obama took prominent roles on the campaign trail on Wednesday, with less than a week to go before congressional races that could shift the balance of power in Washington. Thirty-five ‌of the 100 Senate seats and all 435 seats in the House of Representatives are being contested next Tuesday. Nonpartisan analysts generally favor Democrats' chances of capturing a majority in the ⁠House, with the contest for the Senate seen as very close.

item.title: Minimum wage increase could come early as France braces for protests
item.description: The French government is looking for new ways to calm social unrest ahead of more planned demonstrations over the cost of living this weekend. The minimum wage was set to increase on January 1, 2027. Now, officials are considering making the change one month earlier and adding an extra boost.

item.title: 'Real questions to be asked' after deadly train collision in Spain, journalist says
item.description: In this edition of Perspective, we focus on the tragic train collision that killed at least 68 people in Spain on Wednesday. We're joined by Nicholas Kingsley, executive editor of Railway Gazette International.

item.title: Early vote one week out shows Democratic enthusiasm in Texas, Georgia: Analysis
item.description: With just one week out to the 2026 midterms, an ABC News analysis of the early vote in the key states of Texas and Georgia shows signs of enthusiasm for Democrats.

item.title: Why defeated Flavio Bolsonaro fled Brazil for Miami - and what comes next
item.description: On Wednesday, Flavio Bolsonaro, who last week lost Brazil's presidential election, was seen arriving in the US on a private jet after having fled in the dead of night.

item.description: Get ready to fall back

item.description: The French head of the European Central Bank (ECB) is to step down from the role, just months ahead of the troubled country's presidential election.

item.description: ABC News’ Jay O’Brien talks to Maine Senate candidates Troy Jackson (D) and Sen. Susan Collins (R), as well as to fishermen and loggers impacted by tariffs placed on machinery imported from Canada.

item.title: WATCH: These dogs just love a pile of leaves
item.description: ABC News' Danny New talks to a family from Maine that makes sure their yard always has a leaf pile ready for their two leaf-loving dogs.

item.title: WATCH: 'Liberty Biberty must go!' Protest over car insurance mascot
item.description: A small crowd took to the streets of Boston to protest against the existence of Liberty Biberty, the new fuzzy yellow mascot that appears in the insurance giant Liberty Mutual's TV ads.

item.title: North Korea fires ballistic missiles off east coast as tensions with South rise
item.description: North Korea has launched ballistic missiles off its east coast into the Sea of Japan, South Korea said on Thursday, as tensions continued to rise between the two countries.

item.title: Justice Department announces Trump plans for golf course are in the works
item.description: The Justice Department has filed notice that President Donald Trump’s announcements that there are plans for renovating the East Potomac Golf Course and there are plans to close the park beginning Nov. 15 are accurate

item.title: Judge rejects Trump admin request for order to segregate 20,000 Calif. ballots
item.description: The Justice Department sought an emergency order in the case.

item.description: ABC News’ Linsey Davis speaks with a Long Island couple suing a now-former broker at realtor Douglas Elliman for housing discrimination, after the broker sent a text saying “Ugh they are black.”

item.title: 2 right-wing provocateurs facing election-related charges in Minnesota
item.description: Right-wing provocateurs James O'Keefe and Cam Higby are facing election-related charges after posting videos intended to expose alleged election security deficiencies.

item.title: Girl injured in wolf attack at wildlife park
item.description: An eight-year-old girl has been seriously injured in a wolf attack at a wildlife park in Germany.

item.title: WATCH: David Muir remembers the life and legacy of Barbara Barrie
item.description: The Oscar, Emmy and Tony nominee appeared in numerous films and TV series, including her role as the supportive mother in “Breaking Away.” David Muir remembers her legacy.

item.title: US makes interest rate decision - as Bank of England verdict looms
item.description: The Federal Reserve has left interest rates unchanged - despite persistently high inflation and repeated calls from Donald Trump to lower borrowing costs.

item.title: WATCH: How Trump’s economic policies could shape the midterms
item.description: ABC News’ Alex Presha examines voters’ economic concerns, while KPMG chief economist Diane Swonk discusses interest rates, consumer confidence and financial uncertainty.

item.description: 24/7 coverage of breaking news and live events

item.title: WATCH: Where to find the best deals for Thanksgiving
item.description: With Halloween this weekend, many families are already planning for Thanksgiving, and Rebecca Jarvis is at a turkey farm in New Jersey with ways to save on your Thanksgiving meal.

item.title: WATCH: All eyes on rising prices
item.description: With six days to go, inflation and high gas prices are key concerns for voters.

item.description: ABC News contributor Dr. Alok Patel explains the report and what people can do for treatment and prevention.

item.title: WATCH: Viral explorer finishes 500-mile paddle through Africa
item.description: ABC News' Danny New talks to Ash Dykes, an explorer who kayaked for 500 miles down the Congo Basin in Africa, paddling alongside monkeys and hippos.

item.description: Poundland has filed notice to appoint administrators, bringing it one step closer to collapse.
